key_insight: Stable, physically meaningful elastic-turbulence statistics can still emerge even when local positive-definiteness of the polymer conformation tensor is violated, provided the simulation is above a minimum resolution.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce the computational cost of direct numerical simulations for polymeric flows, making elastic-turbulence studies more accessible on less extreme HPC resources.
method: Simulate a dilute polymer solution in low-Re plane-channel flow using a conformation-tensor formulation.
Compare three resolution regimes: unstable blow-up, chaotic but non-positive-definite, and fully positive-definite.
Check whether key mid-plane statistics remain consistent across the stable regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two resolution thresholds and shows that, in the intermediate regime, velocity, velocity-gradient, and polymer-stretch statistics match fully positive-definite simulations.
watch_item: Local violations of Tr(c)>3 may be acceptable for some statistics, but they still indicate loss of physical positivity and may not be safe for all observables or transient dynamics.
paper_title: No need to stay positive: a practical approach to direct numerical simulations of elastic turbulence
